learning_outcomes.text: Has structured knowledge of the basics of metrology of electrical quantities, legal metrology.
Knows and understands the diagrams of electrical measurement systems.
Can work individually and in a team.
Can develop documentation for the implementation of an engineering task and prepare text or presentation containing a discussion of the results of this task.
Is aware of the responsibility for one's own work and readiness to abide by the rules of teamwork and bear responsibility for jointly implemented tasks.

syllabus_topics: Laboratory classes on: - determining uncertainty, - application of basic measuring instruments, - DC measurement systems, - AC measurement systems.
Basic information about measurement: a. definition of measurement, b. measured quantity, c. value of quantity, d. measurement path, e. concept of transducer.
Units and standards, standardization organizations and documents concerning measurement issues. Legal metrology, international system of units.
Measurement result, measurement errors and uncertainties. Basics of measurement uncertainty analysis.
Compensatory methods for measuring DC voltages and currents. Idea of compensatory measurement, compensation systems for DC voltages.
Electromechanical meters. Construction, operation, and quantities affecting the readings of electromechanical instruments.
Technical measurements with direct current. Measurement of basic quantities in DC circuits using a voltmeter and ammeter.
DC bridges. Idea of DC bridges, measurement of small and large resistances.
Measurement of parameters of alternating waveforms. Definitions of quantities measured for sinusoidal voltage and current signals.
Oscilloscope. Construction and operation of the oscilloscope.
AC bridges. Idea of AC bridges, methods of balancing AC bridges, elimination of basic disturbances in AC bridges.
Measurement of power and energy. Idea of measuring power and electrical energy, basic block diagram of a wattmeter, properties of a single-phase system for power and energy measurement.
Electricity meter. Inductive meter, electronic meter, operating principle and measurement systems.
Measurement of power and energy in three-phase networks. Power and energy measurement systems in 3-phase networks, measurement ideas, diagrams, properties.
Perspectives of building and using classical measurement systems. Summary lecture with emphasis on modern solutions for measuring electrical quantities.
assessment_rules: For lectures, a positive grade from the final colloquium is required. For laboratory classes, all laboratory exercises must be completed, all reports must be passed, and at least 50% of possible points must be obtained. Passing the module is possible after passing all laboratory classes. Student preparation for laboratory exercises may be verified by an oral or written colloquium.
